title: Continuous Calibration Controller for Kernel Choice
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight continuous calibration controller that keeps the runtime's kernel choice policy tuned to real traffic and heterogeneous hardware. The controller should: 1) maintain an online cost-latency model conditioned on hardware fingerprint, sequence-length histogram, quantization profile, and prefill/decode mix; 2) run low-overhead probes and periodic microbenchmarks to update model parameters; 3) coordinate safe rollouts of updated kernel mappings with automatic rollback on SLO regressions. Goal: reduce tail-latency for mixed workloads and avoid stale kernel assignments after infra changes or new model versions.
proposed_approach: 1) Lightweight local agent on each serving node samples short representative microbenchmarks (prefill and decode probes) on idle slots; probes are capped by CPU/GPU usage budget. 2) Agents report summarized metrics (p50, p95, p99 latency, throughput, GPU occupancy, memory headroom) to controller. 3) Controller fits an interpretable cost model (ridge regression + uncertainty via bootstrap) keyed by hardware fingerprint, seq_len_bucket, and model_quantization tag. 4) New kernel recommendations are ranked by expected latency and cost delta with confidence intervals. 5) Staged rollout: canary subset -> ramp -> global, with automatic fallback if p99 or error rate regresses beyond thresholds. 6) Provide a manual override and per-customer pinning in Dedicated/Private modes.
acceptance_criteria: Controller produces kernel recommendations daily and on infra changes
Canary rollout completes without p99 > baseline + 15% or error rate > baseline + 0.1%
End-to-end pipeline adds <1% request overhead in common workloads (probes amortized)
Observed median token-cost improvement >= 5% on mixed-length traffic in experiment A
Documentation: runbook for rollback + config schema published in Confluence
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: probes interfere with hot serving – Mitigation: strict GPU occupancy cap + schedule only on <20% idle windows
Risk: noisy measurements produce oscillation – Mitigation: use exponential smoothing + min time between policy changes
Risk: incorrect hardware fingerprinting after driver updates – Mitigation: detect driver or runtime changes and trigger full recalibration
Risk: customer-specific performance regressions on Dedicated – Mitigation: expose per-customer pin and opt-out policy, default to safe kernels
